newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat drifts to lower close on light volumes.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat drifts to lower close on light volumes.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures drifted amid light volumes to close mostly lower on an overall lack of news, traders said.

"There was a lack of news for wheat," a KCBT trader said. "We saw (KCBT wheat) lose ground today to Minneapolis and Chicago. Our wheat's currently the most expensive of the three and therefore stands to lose more as it comes into competition with an increase in world wheat stocks."
KCBT wheat closed 3-1/4 cents per bushel lower to five cents higher, with Sept down 3-1/4 cents at $4.82-1/2. Dec lost 1-1/2 cents to close at $4.84.
Traders said players had been squaring positions ahead of both the end of the month and the Labor Day holiday.
KCBT estimated Tuesday's wheat futures volume at 31.74 million bushels, down from 43.135 million Monday.

Traders said Farmers Commodities Corp bear-spread 800,000 Dec/Sept bushels even money. Wolcott & Lincoln also bear-spread 500,000 Dec/Sept at 1/2 cent per bushel. Prudential Securities was reported to have sold t least 700,000 Dec bushels, floor sources said.
